literal: Peach charms and mao branches were originally what Han used as supplements; mao and metal were also what Wei properly removed, but when the change from midsummer to New Year's Day began is not clear.
idiomatic: Peach charms and mao branches were Han additions to the rite; mao and the Metal phase were rightly dropped under Wei—yet when the ceremony moved from midsummer to New Year's Day remains unclear.

literal: Song abolished them all, but in various commanderies and counties this rite often still survived.
idiomatic: The Song court abolished the practice entirely, though in many commanderies and counties the old rite still lingered.

literal: The protocol of earlier ages for diplomatic visits and tribute, though often seen in the classics, is incomplete from beginning to end.
idiomatic: Earlier protocols for embassies and tribute appear here and there in the classics, but never in a complete account from start to finish.

literal: The Biography of Shusun Tong records the New Year's court audience rite Tong formulated for Han; the outline is broadly sketched, and applied today it is still not complete.
idiomatic: Shusun Tong's biography preserves the Han New Year's audience he devised—only a rough outline—and even by the present day the rite remained incomplete.

literal: When Wei was first established, many matters were incomplete, so only in the third year of Huangchu did they first present jade discs and offer New Year's congratulations.
idiomatic: Wei in its founding years left much undone; not until Huangchu 3 did the court first present jade and receive New Year's homage.

literal: He Chengtian says that no Wei New Year's audience rite survives.
idiomatic: He Chengtian notes that no record of Wei's New Year's audience survives.

literal: Examining He Zhen's Rhapsody on the Capital at Xu, it says: "On New Year's Day the grand feast; the altar stands in the southwest.
idiomatic: He Zhen's Rhapsody on the Capital at Xu reads: "On New Year's Day the grand feast is held; the altar stands in the southwest.

literal: Banners and tents tower high; eaves and halls are vast and deep.
idiomatic: Banners and pavilions rise in lofty rows; eaves and halls stretch wide and deep.

literal: " Wang Shen's Rhapsody on the Proper Audience also says: "Splendid canopies mirror the flying clouds; red curtains spread before the forecourt.
idiomatic: Wang Shen's Rhapsody on the Proper Audience adds: "Splendid canopies gleam against the flying clouds; crimson curtains open across the forecourt.

literal: Blue-green curtains are strung across the two flights of steps, emulating the purple apex's towering grandeur.
idiomatic: Azure curtains span the twin stairways, evoking the lofty majesty of the Purple Apex.

literal: The hundred ministers are summoned to the Gate of Harmony; equals and inferiors alike present their jade tablets.
idiomatic: The hundred ministers gather at the Gate of Harmony, high and low alike bearing jade tablets in tribute.

literal: " From this, the grand feast was entirely outside the city walls, not within the palace.
idiomatic: By these accounts the grand feast was held entirely outside the walls, not within the palace.

literal: Your subject notes that Wei Minister of Works Wang Lang's memorial says: "By precedent, on the first day of the first month, congratulations are offered.
idiomatic: Your subject finds in a memorial by Wang Lang, Minister of Works under Wei: "By established precedent, on the first day of the first month homage is paid.

literal: Two hundred ornate lamps are set below the hall, facing each other between the two flights of steps.
idiomatic: Two hundred decorated lamps are placed beneath the hall, facing one another between the twin stairways.

literal: At the Main Gate court braziers and torches are set up; outside the Main Gate five-foot and three-foot lamps are placed.
idiomatic: Court braziers and torches are lit at the Main Gate, and outside it lamps of five and three feet are arranged.

literal: Moonlight and starlight shine so bright that though it is night, it is like day.
idiomatic: Moon and stars blaze so brightly that night becomes as day.

literal: " Thus, it was not outside the city walls.
idiomatic: On this evidence the ceremony was not held outside the walls.

literal: The two rhapsodies by He and Wang were not originally about Luoyang.
idiomatic: Neither He's nor Wang's rhapsody originally described Luoyang.

literal: He called his the Rhapsody on the Capital at Xu—at the time they were at Xuchang.
idiomatic: He titled his work the Rhapsody on the Capital at Xu, for the court was then at Xuchang.

literal: Wang's rhapsody also says "audience with the four states on the eastern tour"—also a rhapsody on Xuchang's proper audience.
idiomatic: Wang's poem likewise speaks of "receiving the four states on the eastern progress"—another account of Xuchang's formal New Year's audience.

literal: In Emperor Wu of Jin's reign, the regulations for the New Year's audience were revised; the present Xianning commentary is that revision.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Jin the New Year's audience was re-regulated; the Xianning commentary that survives is that revision.

literal: Fu Xuan's Rhapsody on the New Year's Audience says: "Examining the surviving instructions of Xia, surveying the canonical arts of Yin and Zhou, gathering the old rites of Qin and Han, he fixed the auspicious assembly of New Year's Day.
idiomatic: Fu Xuan's Rhapsody on the New Year's Audience says: "Drawing on Xia's surviving teachings, weighing the canonical arts of Yin and Zhou, and collecting Qin and Han precedent, he established the great assembly of New Year's Day.

literal: From this one can see that it drew from many dynasties.
idiomatic: This shows plainly that the rite combined practices from many ages.

literal: The Xianning commentary: First, on the first day of the first month, the palace guard overnight sets out folding seats for kings, dukes, ministers, and senior officials outside the Main Gate; the Directorate of Music and the Drum-and-Pipe office also overnight set up music from four sides and ox-and-horse tents and pavilions before the hall.
idiomatic: The Xianning commentary begins: On the first day of the first month, the palace guard spends the night arranging folding seats outside the Main Gate for kings, dukes, ministers, and senior officials; the Directorate of Music and Drum-and-Pipe office likewise prepare music on four sides and ox-and-horse pavilions before the hall.

literal: Before the night clepsydra has run out ten quarters, the assembled ministers arrive, and the court braziers are lit.
idiomatic: Before ten night watches remain on the clepsydra, the ministers assemble and the court braziers are kindled.

literal: The emperor offers congratulations and receives the response; he then congratulates the empress.
idiomatic: The emperor pays his respects and receives the formal reply, then offers New Year's congratulations to the empress.

literal: Returning, he enters through the Cloud Dragon Gate's eastern Zhonghua Gate to offer congratulations, then goes to the folding seats below the eastern pavilion.
idiomatic: He returns by the eastern Zhonghua Gate of the Cloud Dragon Gate to pay homage, then takes a folding seat beneath the eastern pavilion.

literal: Before the clepsydra has run out seven quarters, the various offices by carriage and all officials down to the tribute-receiving attendants and the accounting clerks all enter and take position at the foot of the steps.
idiomatic: With seven watches still remaining, officials of every office arrive by carriage, together with all ranks down to tribute attendants and accounting clerks, and take their places at the foot of the steps.

literal: Those guarding the steps follow the protocol for audience at the front hall.
idiomatic: The step guards observe the same protocol used for an audience at the front hall.

literal: Before the clepsydra has run out five quarters, the Chief Usher and Grand Master of Ceremonies each announce: "The assembled ministers are in place.
idiomatic: With five watches left, the Chief Usher and Grand Master of Ceremonies each report: "The assembled ministers are in position.

literal: " When the clepsydra runs out, the Attendant Within announces: "Outside is ready.
idiomatic: When the clepsydra empties, the Attendant Within reports: "All is ready outside.

literal: " The emperor emerges.
idiomatic: The emperor then comes forth.

literal: Bells and drums sound; all officials bow and prostrate.
idiomatic: Bells and drums strike; every official bows to the ground.

literal: The Minister of Ceremonies leads the emperor to ascend the imperial throne.
idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies guides the emperor up to the imperial throne.

literal: Bells and drums cease.
idiomatic: The bells and drums fall silent.

literal: All officials rise.
idiomatic: The officials rise.

literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies kneels and announces: "We request the New Year's audience.
idiomatic: The Grand Master of Ceremonies kneels and petitions: "We beg to begin the New Year's audience.

literal: " The Director of Ritual intones: "The emperor invites the kings to ascend.
idiomatic: The Director of Ritual calls out: "The emperor invites the kings to ascend.

literal: " The Grand Master of Ceremonies kneels and intones: "The feudal kings, subjects So-and-so and others, present one white jade disc each and bow twice in congratulation.
idiomatic: The Grand Master of Ceremonies kneels and announces: "The feudal kings, your subjects So-and-so and the rest, each present one white jade disc and bow twice in congratulation.

literal: " The Minister of Ceremonies responds: "All kings may ascend.
idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies replies: "Let all the kings ascend.

literal: " An usher leads them up the hall to face the imperial throne.
idiomatic: Ushers lead them up the hall to stand before the throne.

literal: The emperor rises; the kings bow twice.
idiomatic: The emperor stands; the kings bow twice.

literal: The emperor sits; they bow twice again, kneel and place the jade before the throne, and bow twice again.
idiomatic: When the emperor is seated they bow again, kneel to set the jade before the throne, and bow twice more.

literal: When the rite is complete, the usher leads them down the hall and back to their original positions.
idiomatic: Once the ceremony is finished, the usher conducts them down the hall and back to their places.

literal: The Director of Ritual leads dukes, specially advanced worthies, the son of the Southern Xiongnu Chanyu, and generals with gold seal and purple cord to the west of the Grand Master of Ceremonies; those of middle-second-rank, second-rank, first-rank, and sixth-rank salary to the west of the Director of Great Processions—all facing north and prostrating.
idiomatic: The Director of Ritual places dukes, specially advanced officials, the son of the Southern Xiongnu Chanyu, and gold-seal generals with purple cords west of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, and middle-second-rank officials through sixth-rank salary west of the Director of Great Processions—all facing north and prostrate.

literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies kneels and intones: "The Grand Commandant, middle-second-rank officials, and others present jade discs, leather, silk, lambs, geese, and pheasants, and bow twice in congratulation.
idiomatic: The Grand Master of Ceremonies kneels and announces: "The Grand Commandant, middle-second-rank officials, and the rest present jade, leather, silk, lambs, geese, and pheasants, and bow twice in congratulation.

literal: " The Minister of Ceremonies intones: "The emperor invites you, lords, to ascend.
idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies calls: "The emperor invites you, my lords, to ascend.

literal: " The Director of Ritual leads dukes through generals with gold seal and purple cord up the hall to face the throne.
idiomatic: The Director of Ritual leads the dukes through the gold-seal generals up the hall to stand before the throne.

literal: The emperor rises; all bow twice.
idiomatic: The emperor rises; all bow twice.

literal: The emperor sits; they bow twice again.
idiomatic: When he is seated they bow twice again.

literal: Kneeling, they place the jade discs and leather and silk before the throne and bow twice again.
idiomatic: They kneel, set the jade and silk offerings before the throne, and bow twice more.

literal: When the rite is complete, the intoner leads them down the hall and back to their positions.
idiomatic: After the ceremony the announcer leads them down the hall and back to their stations.

literal: When kings and dukes placed their jade and completed the rite, the Director of Great Processions intoned together; below the hall, middle-second-rank and below followed the same.
idiomatic: While kings and dukes presented their jade, the Director of Great Processions joined in the announcements; below the hall, middle-second-rank officials and those beneath them did likewise.

literal: When the rite was complete, the tribute was handed to the tribute-receiving attendants; the attendants passed the jade and silk to the ushers, and the lambs, geese, and pheasants to the Director of the Palace Kitchen.
idiomatic: Once the ceremony ended, the tribute gifts went to the receiving attendants, who passed jade and silk to the ushers and the lambs, geese, and pheasants to the Director of the Palace Kitchen.

literal: The Director of Music kneels and requests that court music be performed.
idiomatic: The Director of Music kneels and asks that court music be played.

literal: Music is performed in sequence.
idiomatic: The music is performed in turn.

literal: The Director of Imperial Carriages then brings out the chariots.
idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Carriages then has the chariots brought out.

literal: The emperor withdraws; all officials take their seats.
idiomatic: The emperor retires within, and the officials all take their seats.

literal: At the sixth quarter of the day clepsydra's rising water, the various barbarian and foreign guests enter in order; all bow twice and sit.
idiomatic: At the sixth watch of the day clepsydra, barbarian and foreign guests enter in succession, each bowing twice before taking a seat.

literal: At the third quarter of the emperor's entry, he emerges again.
idiomatic: Three watches into the emperor's withdrawal, he comes out again.

literal: Bells and drums sound.
idiomatic: Bells and drums strike once more.

literal: The Chief Usher kneels and announces: "We request that the assembled ministers ascend.
idiomatic: The Chief Usher kneels and petitions: "We beg the assembled ministers to ascend.

literal: " The ushers lead kings, dukes, and second-rank officials up the hall; first-rank and sixth-rank officials remain in their positions.
idiomatic: Ushers conduct kings, dukes, and second-rank officials up the hall, while first-rank and sixth-rank officials remain at their posts.

literal: An usher leads a king to the honored place to pour longevity wine, kneels and hands it to the Attendant Within.
idiomatic: An usher guides a king to the place of honor to pour longevity wine, kneels, and presents it to the Attendant Within.

literal: The Attendant Within kneels and places it before the throne.
idiomatic: The Attendant Within kneels and sets it before the throne.

literal: The king returns, pours for himself, and places it before his seat.
idiomatic: The king withdraws, pours for himself, and places the cup before his own seat.

literal: An usher kneels and announces: "The feudal kings, subjects So-and-so and others, present the cup and bow twice, offering congratulations for ten thousand years of life.
idiomatic: An usher kneels and announces: "The feudal kings, your subjects So-and-so and the rest, raise the cup, bow twice, and wish ten thousand years of life.

literal: " The Attendant Within says: "The cup has been presented.
idiomatic: The Attendant Within declares: "The cup has been offered.

literal: " All officials prostrate and shout "Ten thousand years!"
idiomatic: All officials prostrate and cry, "Ten thousand years!"

literal: Music from the four sides plays.
idiomatic: Music rises from all four sides.

literal: All officials bow twice.
idiomatic: The officials bow twice.

literal: Having drunk, they bow twice again.
idiomatic: After drinking, they bow twice again.

literal: The ushers lead the various kings and others back to their positions.
idiomatic: Ushers conduct the kings and the rest back to their places.

literal: The step attendants relay the command to take seats; all ministers kneel and assent.
idiomatic: Attendants at the steps pass the order to be seated, and the ministers kneel in assent.

literal: The Attendant Within, Director of the Secretariat, and Director of the Department of State Affairs each present longevity wine in the hall; the ascending-song music rises, and the Director of the Palace Kitchen also serves the imperial wine.
idiomatic: The Attendant Within, Director of the Secretariat, and Director of the Department of State Affairs each offer longevity wine in the hall; the ascending song begins, and the Director of the Palace Kitchen serves the emperor's wine.

literal: The imperial wine ascends the steps; the Director of the Palace Kitchen kneels and hands it to the Vice Director, who kneels and presents it before the throne.
idiomatic: The imperial wine is carried up the steps; the Director of the Palace Kitchen kneels and passes it to a Vice Director, who kneels and presents it before the throne.

literal: Then wine is served to all officials.
idiomatic: Wine is then served to all the officials.

literal: The Director of Music kneels and announces: "Perform the ascending song.
idiomatic: The Director of Music kneels and reports: "Play the ascending song.

literal: " Three times.
idiomatic: Three times.

literal: When it ends, they descend.
idiomatic: When the performance ends, the musicians descend.

literal: The Director of the Palace Kitchen kneels and requests that the imperial meal be brought to the steps; all ministers rise.
idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Kitchen kneels to announce that the imperial meal has reached the steps, and all the ministers rise.

literal: The Director of the Palace Kitchen holds the soup and kneels to hand it to the Minister of Education;
idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Kitchen holds the soup, kneels, and presents it to the Minister of Education;

literal: holds the rice and kneels to hand it to the Minister of Revenue;
idiomatic: holds the rice, kneels, and presents it to the Minister of Revenue;

literal: the Director of Imperial Cuisine holds the tray and together hands it to the Vice Director, who kneels and presents it before the throne.
idiomatic: and the Director of Imperial Cuisine carries the tray and, together with a Vice Director, kneels to present it before the throne.

literal: All ministers take their seats.
idiomatic: The ministers take their seats.

literal: The Director of Music kneels and announces: "While eating,
idiomatic: The Director of Music kneels and announces: "While the meal is taken,

literal: raise the music."
idiomatic: let music be raised."

literal: The Director of the Palace Kitchen distributes meal trays to all officials throughout.
idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Kitchen sends meal trays to every official in turn.

literal: When the meal is finished, the Director of Music kneels and announces: "We request that dancers enter.
idiomatic: When the meal is finished, the Director of Music kneels and petitions: "We beg that the dancers be brought in.

literal: " Dances are performed in sequence.
idiomatic: The dances are performed one after another.

literal: The Director of Drum-and-Pipe likewise advances and kneels to announce: "We request that the various performers enter in order.
idiomatic: The Director of Drum-and-Pipe likewise steps forward, kneels, and asks: "We beg that the various performers enter in turn.

literal: " Then the accounting clerks from all commanderies are summoned forward and receive imperial instructions and admonitions at the foot of the steps.
idiomatic: The accounting clerks from every commandery are then called forward and receive the emperor's charge and admonition at the foot of the steps.

literal: When the banquet and music are finished, one usher kneels and announces: "We request dismissal.
idiomatic: When the banquet and music are complete, a single usher kneels and petitions: "We beg leave to withdraw.

literal: " Bells and drums sound; all ministers face north, bow twice, and withdraw.
idiomatic: Bells and drums sound; the ministers turn north, bow twice, and depart.

literal: In the lands south of the Yangzi they further adjusted positions according to circumstances, but in the main there was little difference.
idiomatic: South of the Yangzi positions were adjusted case by case, yet the overall form differed little.

literal: When Song possessed the realm, it largely kept the old rites; what was reduced or increased can be seen.
idiomatic: Once Song held the empire it mostly retained the old ceremonies, and the additions and cuts are plain enough.

literal: In the Jin commentary for the lands south of the Yangzi, when the crown prince attended the assembly, he stood below the Three Honored Ones and above kings and dukes.
idiomatic: The Jin regulations for the south placed the crown prince, when he attended, below the Three Honored Ones but above kings and dukes.

literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, he was raised above the Three Honored Ones.
idiomatic: In Yuanjia 11 under Emperor Wen of Song, the crown prince was moved above the Three Honored Ones.

literal: Under Wei regulations, feudal kings were not permitted to attend court audiences.
idiomatic: Wei law forbade feudal kings from coming to court for audience.

literal: When some did attend under Emperor Ming, it was entirely by special grace and could not be taken as the rule.
idiomatic: Those who appeared at court under Emperor Ming did so only by special favor and could not be treated as precedent.
